doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: Arrangers Holiday and the summer trumpet section
summary: At Eastman's Arrangers Holiday he sight-read and recorded, leading a section of Mosello, Tyzik and Vizutti.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Oh I love Rochester. I haven’t been back since I taught at Eastman, summers. Did you go to the Arrangers Holiday at all?
That was one of my favorite things to do.
Because we sight read music and then we recorded it immediately.
So it was always a challenge. And the trumpet section, my favorite trumpet section was I played, Joe Mosello, Jeff Tyzik, and Al Vizutti.

That was the summer section. And it was great because I was sort of the lead trumpet at the time. And I’d say, “Al, you’ve got to play this one. This one is — we’re only going to do it twice” I said, “we want to get a good recording for this guy,” I said, “I might mess this funny technique place up.” You know? “Oh, okay.” And he’d just kill it. I mean you could turn the music upside down and he could read it. Allen Vizutti could play, because he played the way I’m talking about only his mind was like ten times faster than mine could ever be. And you know Jeff Tyzik could play like the stuff that was more contemporary sounding, you know like the latest kind of fusion stuff. And Joe was a player like me. So we would switch off and then we’d all switch off. When we played shows none of us played strictly lead, even though at the time the lead trumpet in Rochester musicians union, I refused to play first trumpet after a while. Because you got paid the same amount and they had these people — they had people that were working in the theater every week when it was easy. And they’d only call me or Al or Jeff or somebody, you know what I mean, when it was too hard.
